design.role: Welcome transit host; food, beds, local meeting point, and temporary caravan drop point
design.background: He arrived in Welcome years ago with a caravan and intended to stay only briefly. A mundane delay became temporary work, then responsibility, then a life. He can still joke that he is only passing through even though the community treats him as local.
personality: helpful without making a performance of it
skeptical of grand promises but invested in ordinary life
speech_style: rarely explains world facts the player character should already know
uses ordinary work and people as context instead of lore lectures
gameplay_purposes: one access point into the workshop-package situation
later equipment-aware reaction to the workshop boots
narrative_purposes: show that Welcome is a functioning lived-in place
embody someone who stayed without turning that choice into a philosophy lecture
make caravan dependence understandable before the important caravan fails to arrive
be someone the player expects to see again rather than an obvious farewell character

relationships.notes: The workshop package can be discovered from either side. The Traveler currently holds the workshop materials at the inn.

relationships.working_label: The one who does not attach
relationships.notes: Possible older connection from before or during arrival at Welcome. Not frozen.

beats.title: First meeting

lines.text: If you're looking for food, there is some. A bed — maybe. Work? Somehow, there's always work.

beats.notes: Any completed first-meeting choice records that this character has met the NPC.

lines.text: Food, beds, people arriving too late and people leaving too early. Stay a little and you'll understand.

beats.title: Only passing through
beats.notes: The joke gains meaning only if the player later learns how long he has lived here.

beats.title: Workshop package — craftsperson not yet met

lines.text: The workshop's things have been sitting here for two days. If you're heading that way, save us a trip.

beats.notes: This path allows the player to discover the workshop situation through the inn before ever visiting the workshop.

beats.title: Workshop package — craftsperson already met

lines.text: Ah, he already sent you? Good. His things have been sitting here for two days.

choices.text: Give it here. I'm heading that way.

beats.notes: Same world situation, different framing because the player reached the workshop first.

beats.title: Workshop package contents

lines.text: Leather, buckles, sole pieces. Nothing exciting until you have to walk all day with a torn shoe.

beats.notes: Optional conversational freedom without a different world outcome.

beats.title: Important caravan expected today

lines.text: The caravan should come in today. Food, medicine, gear for the guards. About time — we're starting to scrape the bottom of a few shelves.

beats.notes: Continuity setup. This should sound routine, not like disaster foreshadowing.

beats.title: Important caravan is clearly late

lines.text: They should've been here by now.

beats.notes: Later content may distinguish slightly-late from concerning-late.

beats.title: How Welcome changed

lines.text: When I arrived, there were three roofs here. Two of them leaked.
There are more roofs now. Some still leak.

beats.notes: Optional lore; hearing it must never be required to progress through Welcome.

beats.title: Normal filler
beats.notes: Repeatable filler that does not advance progression.

notes: The workshop package is a pre-existing world situation. Neither the Traveler nor the workshop craftsperson owns or starts it.
Welcome initialization should begin with welcome.workshop.package_needed=true, welcome.workshop.package_at_inn=true, and welcome.workshop.package_delivered=false.
Taking the package changes package_at_inn to false. Delivery at the workshop changes package_delivered to true and package_needed to false.
NPC knowledge must not automatically equal all character/world facts.
Shared physical NPC activity versus per-client conversational gestures remains a future runtime/presentation concern.
